title: Bug: notebooklm_notebooks_list can serve stale source_count until MCP server restart
description:
## Summary
`notebooklm_notebooks_list` reported `source_count=0` for live notebooks even though the same notebooks contained sources.

The current workspace code does not reproduce the parser bug anymore. The mismatch is caused by the running MCP server process holding older code in memory after local source changes.

Observed on 2026-03-07.

## Evidence
### MCP tool results from the running server
- `notebooklm_notebooks_list` returned:
  - `e862eaf0-6c7d-43ca-822a-41278e9f2ef5` -> `source_count=0`
  - `d9b32097-ff19-4d0c-a3b8-d87cac6c1c1d` -> `source_count=0`
- `notebooklm_sources_list` for the same notebooks returned:
  - `e862eaf0-6c7d-43ca-822a-41278e9f2ef5` -> 5 sources
  - `d9b32097-ff19-4d0c-a3b8-d87cac6c1c1d` -> 3 sources

### Direct workspace SDK/raw checks
Using `NotebookLMClient.from_storage()` from the current workspace source tree:
- `client.notebooks.list()` returned:
  - `e862eaf0-6c7d-43ca-822a-41278e9f2ef5` -> `sources_count=5`
  - `d9b32097-ff19-4d0c-a3b8-d87cac6c1c1d` -> `sources_count=3`
- `client.notebooks.get_raw(id)` showed `len(data[1])` of 5 and 3 respectively.

### Runtime drift evidence
- Running server process: `uv run notebooklm-mcp serve --http -v`
- Process start time observed at approximately `2026-03-07 09:13` local time.
- Current workspace file [src/notebooklm/types.py] already includes a local `sources_count = len(data[1])` parse and returns it from `Notebook.from_api_response()`.
- `git blame` on those lines shows local uncommitted edits newer than the server start time, indicating the server loaded pre-fix code and was never restarted.

## Root Cause Analysis
The running `notebooklm-mcp` process was started before the local `sources_count` parser fix existed. Python loaded the old module state into memory at process start. After the workspace source changed, direct SDK calls from the current checkout used the updated code path, but the already-running MCP server continued serving the old in-memory implementation.

This means the observed wrong count is an operational/version-drift bug in the running server, not a current parser bug in the workspace source.

## Impact
- User-visible notebook metadata is inconsistent across tools.
- Agents can make incorrect decisions based on `source_count` from `notebooklm_notebooks_list`.
- Closed bug `bd-16k` no longer reflects the current root cause and can mislead future debugging.

## Proposed Fix
1. Restart/redeploy `notebooklm-mcp` after parser/tool-output code changes.
2. Add startup/runtime diagnostics that expose loaded code version, commit, or source fingerprint so stale processes are obvious.
3. Add an ops/smoke check that can detect drift between notebook list counts and live source inventory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- After restarting the MCP server, `notebooklm_notebooks_list` returns non-zero counts matching `client.notebooks.list()` and `notebooklm_sources_list`.
- The server exposes enough runtime version/fingerprint information to diagnose stale-process drift quickly.
- Documentation or diagnostics make it clear that hot code edits require a server restart for MCP behavior changes to take effect.
close_reason: Resolved

title: Upgrade notebooklm-mcp into an evidence-first BA implementation pack runner
description:
Background:
`notebooklm-py` already exposes broad NotebookLM primitives, but the repository does not yet provide a workflow-native orchestration layer that can turn BA PDFs and supporting sources into deterministic implementation packs. This umbrella epic tracks the full upgrade program from foundation work through QA hardening and optional parity.

Scope:
- Land the critical-path phases described in `notebooklm_mcp_upgrade_plan_revised.md`.
- Keep the implementation single-user, non-sharing, and local-first by default.
- Preserve a clean separation between generic NotebookLM MCP parity work and the BA-specific runner.
- Treat documentation, tests, and rerun economics as first-class deliverables rather than polish.

Deliverables:
- A coherent `br` graph for the upgrade program.
- A dedicated BA runner subsystem and public `ba.*` MCP surface.
- Deterministic bundle generation with validation and incremental rerun support.
- Docs and fixtures that let future contributors understand and extend the workflow safely.

## Success Criteria
- All child epics that define the core workflow are closed with repository evidence.
- The workflow can ingest typed sources, extract canonical facts, render FE/BE bundles, validate outputs, and rerun impacted screens only.
- Optional parity work is clearly scoped so it cannot dilute the main BA-runner outcome.

Non-Goals:
- Building a multi-user collaboration product.
- Replacing the existing MCP server with a separate application.
- Treating optional artifact parity as the primary business outcome.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Future-self guidance:
- Protect the critical path. If tradeoffs become necessary, slip optional parity before weakening evidence tracking, canonical schemas, or bundle validation.
- The upgrade only succeeds if the final system is honest about uncertainty. Provisional contracts, degraded parses, and contradictory sources must remain explicit.
- Do not let this epic devolve into 'expose more tools.' The real product is the workflow runner and its deterministic output contract.

title: Phase 0: audit parity and lay the BA runner foundations
description:
Background:
Before adding new BA workflow behavior, the repo needs a grounded view of current MCP vs SDK capability coverage and a stable internal architecture for the new subsystem. This phase prevents later rework caused by building on guessed capabilities or by scattering BA logic across existing generic modules.

Scope:
- Audit the current MCP surface against the `notebooklm-py` capabilities required by the BA workflow.
- Define the package boundaries for the BA subsystem and keep generic tool modules from becoming the dumping ground for new logic.
- Stand up the core adapter, schema, storage, and fixture scaffolding needed by later phases.

Deliverables:
- Parity matrix with concrete call-site notes.
- `src/notebooklm_mcp/ba/` package skeleton and architecture boundaries.
- Adapter, model, run-store, and fixture scaffolding foundations.

## Success Criteria
- Later phases can build inside a dedicated BA subsystem without relocating major modules.
- The team knows which upstream capabilities already exist, which need exposing, and which are unstable or absent.
- Schema and storage decisions are settled enough to support real downstream implementation.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Sequencing note:
- This phase exists to buy down architectural and capability uncertainty.
- If it is skipped or rushed, the likely failure mode is not 'a missing feature'; it is a fragmented implementation spread across ad hoc helpers that later becomes expensive to reason about.

title: Audit current MCP parity against the NotebookLM capabilities the BA workflow actually needs
description:
Background:
The revised plan assumes `notebooklm-py` already exposes most raw capabilities the BA runner needs, while the current MCP surface is narrower. This task makes that assumption concrete so later work can target real gaps instead of anecdotes from README prose.

Scope:
- Inspect the SDK, CLI, current MCP tools/resources/prompts, and docs for source, note, settings, research, artifact, and export coverage relevant to the BA workflow.
- Record which capabilities are already exposed cleanly, which need adapter work only, which need new MCP surface area, and which are unstable or unclear.
- Ground the audit in repo code paths, not just marketing-level documentation.

Deliverables:
- Parity matrix with capability, repo location, current MCP exposure state, and notes on whether it is critical, helpful, optional, or experimental for the BA runner.
- A short list of must-have call sites for the capability adapter.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The team can point to a concrete artifact showing what exists today and what is missing for the BA workflow.
- Later phase tasks can reference this audit instead of rediscovering SDK/MCP gaps ad hoc.

Non-Goals:
- Implementing new BA workflow behavior directly.
close_reason: Completed: parity audit landed in docs/ba-runner-parity-audit.md

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Implementation guidance:
- Prefer evidence from `src/notebooklm/`, `src/notebooklm_mcp/`, and tests over assumptions from the README.
- Pay special attention to source fulltext/guide/freshness, note conversion, output language, reports, data tables, and artifact exports because those directly influence the workflow design.

title: Carve out a dedicated `src/notebooklm_mcp/ba/` subsystem and module boundaries
description:
Background:
The existing MCP code already has sizable generic modules, especially `tools/workflows.py`. This task exists to prevent the BA runner from becoming another layer of ad hoc logic inside those files.

Scope:
- Define the internal package split for models, adapter, run store, prompt registry, extraction, rendering, validation, reruns, and tool entry points.
- Keep generic NotebookLM parity concerns separated from BA-runner concerns.
- Create the skeleton in a way that later phases can fill in incrementally without moving files around again.

Deliverables:
- Dedicated `src/notebooklm_mcp/ba/` package skeleton or equivalent architecture with clear module ownership.
- Notes or lightweight ADR-style guidance on why the boundaries exist.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Later work can land in the BA subsystem without increasing coupling to generic tool modules.
- The boundaries are clear enough that contributors know where new workflow logic belongs.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Future-self warning:
- Resist the temptation to put 'just one helper' into existing generic files unless it is truly generic. Repeating that convenience is how the codebase becomes impossible to reason about.

title: Implement a capability adapter skeleton over the `NotebookLMClient` surface
description:
Background:
The BA runner should not call raw SDK methods throughout the codebase. It needs a semantic adapter that isolates workflow code from naming changes, transport quirks, and parity differences between SDK, CLI, and MCP layers.

Scope:
- Define the adapter interface in terms of workflow needs: source ingest, snapshot data retrieval, structured ask helpers, notes, settings, and artifact support.
- Hide direct SDK details from later BA modules.
- Return explicit unsupported/degraded states where the upstream surface is absent or unstable.

Deliverables:
- Adapter class or module with typed methods and tests using fakes/stubs.
- Clear guidance that later BA modules talk to the adapter rather than directly to `NotebookLMClient`.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The BA subsystem has one obvious seam for upstream capability calls.
- Unsupported capability handling is centralized instead of being improvised by each workflow step.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Sequencing rationale:
- This adapter is the main hedge against upstream API drift and MCP surface churn.
- It should normalize data and failure modes, not become a second orchestrator.

title: Establish shared BA models, enums, and schema-versioning rules
description:
Background:
Canonical data is the safety rail of the whole design. This task defines the models that source intelligence, extraction, rendering, and validation all share so that the workflow has a single internal language instead of many incompatible intermediate shapes.

Scope:
- Model source manifest rows, evidence objects, terminology entries, screen catalog objects, canonical facts, readiness summaries, contracts, and validator outputs.
- Define enum values and schema-versioning conventions early enough that downstream outputs can depend on them.
- Keep the schemas precise enough for deterministic rendering and validation.

Deliverables:
- Pydantic model package with versioned schemas and unit tests.
- A documented rule for when schema versions must change.

Acceptance Criteria:
- All downstream workflow stages can consume the same typed models.
- Schema changes become intentional and reviewable rather than accidental breakage.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Future-self note:
- Be strict here. Loose models create false velocity and later make renderers and validators brittle.
- Evidence requirements must be encoded in the data model, not only in prose docs.

title: Implement run-store and BA fixture scaffolding foundations
description:
Background:
The workflow depends on durable run metadata, stored snapshots, raw responses, and fixture sets that simulate real BA conditions. This task lays the filesystem and test scaffolding that later phases build on.

Scope:
- Define the on-disk run layout for metadata, prompts, raw responses, snapshots, normalized evidence, and impacted-screen reports.
- Create helper utilities for creating and loading run roots in tests.
- Stand up the initial BA fixture directory structure called for in the revised plan.

Deliverables:
- Run-store skeleton with create/load helpers and typed metadata.
- Fixture directory skeleton for clean, missing-contract, contradictory, garbled, rerun, and note-derived scenarios.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Later workflow steps can persist and reload structured state without inventing storage rules ad hoc.
- The test suite has a stable place to accumulate realistic BA fixtures.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Rationale:
- Cheap reruns and honest audits are impossible without durable run-state and snapshot storage.
- Treat fixture work as production infrastructure for the workflow, not as a nice-to-have test convenience.

title: Phase 1: implement source intelligence and trustworthy inputs
description:
Background:
The BA runner cannot produce trustworthy implementation packs unless it can prove what sources were supplied, how they were typed, whether they were fully ingested, and whether the resulting text is good enough to build on. This phase converts raw source handling into an auditable source intelligence layer.

Scope:
- Normalize typed source registration before execution begins.
- Collapse ingest, polling, snapshotting, and quality assessment into durable workflow primitives.
- Produce an authoritative manifest that later phases can audit and reference.

Deliverables:
- Source registration, ingest-and-wait, snapshotting, parse-quality, and manifest outputs.
- Run-store records that prove exactly what text and metadata were used for extraction.

## Success Criteria
- A run can register, ingest, snapshot, and assess sources without manual glue logic.
- The workflow can halt or degrade explicitly when source quality is insufficient.
- The resulting manifest is suitable as an audit artifact and input to later extraction phases.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Future-self note:
- This phase is where trust starts. If snapshots, hashes, and quality states are weak, every later markdown file will look more certain than it deserves to be.
- Prefer deterministic heuristics here; this layer should not itself become another LLM-dependent mystery box.

title: Implement typed source registration and manifest-row normalization
description:
Background:
Before a run starts ingesting content, it needs a stable and typed record of the user's source intent. This task turns ad hoc source inputs into normalized manifest rows that later phases can rely on.

Scope:
- Accept the source types, priorities, stable keys, and notes described in the plan.
- Validate required primary sources and flag missing critical inputs early.
- Preserve stable `source_key` identity across reruns.

Deliverables:
- Source registration logic and manifest-row model population.
- Warnings for missing critical source categories or malformed source entries.

Acceptance Criteria:
- A run can persist a normalized source manifest before ingestion begins.
- Reruns can reuse source keys without losing audit continuity.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Future-self note:
- The user intent layer matters because later workflow bugs often come from 'we uploaded the wrong thing' rather than from extraction itself.
- Stable source keys are essential for meaningful diffs and reruns.

title: Implement ingest-and-wait orchestration with degraded timeout handling
description:
Background:
Current agent workflows should not have to manually upload sources, poll, and guess when it is safe to continue. This task creates a single source-ingest primitive that absorbs waiting and timeout policy into the workflow itself.

Scope:
- Upload selected sources and poll until they are ready or a budget is exhausted.
- Return explicit per-source degraded states instead of silently continuing after timeout or error.
- Use the adapter and existing MCP concurrency controls rather than ad hoc polling code.

Deliverables:
- Ingest-and-wait operation with bounded polling and status reporting.
- Structured timeout/error payloads that later orchestration can interpret.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The workflow can ingest sources without caller-side wait loops.
- Timeouts or failures are visible and machine-readable at the source level.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Guidance:
- The goal is not just convenience. Centralized waiting eliminates a large class of operator mistakes and makes orchestration easier to reason about.

title: Persist source snapshots, guides, freshness metadata, and content hashes
description:
Background:
The workflow needs to know exactly what text and metadata NotebookLM used at extraction time. This task captures snapshot artifacts that later support audits, validation, and selective reruns.

Scope:
- Store the fulltext used for extraction, plus source guide and freshness data where available.
- Compute stable content hashes for diffing and rerun detection.
- Persist snapshot metadata in the run store with links back to source manifest rows.

Deliverables:
- Snapshot persistence code and metadata schema.
- Content hashing and storage conventions suitable for later diffing.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Every extraction step can reference a concrete snapshot instead of a moving live source.
- The run store can later compare source versions meaningfully.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Future-self note:
- This task is one of the foundations of rerun economics. If snapshot identity is weak, impacted reruns will either miss change or rerun everything.

comments.author: Codex
comments.text: Planning revision: snapshotting is now explicitly blocked on ingest-and-wait so the source audit chain matches the documented register -> ingest -> snapshot -> quality -> manifest flow.

title: Implement deterministic parse-quality heuristics and degradation policy
description:
Background:
A garbled or weakly parsed BA PDF can poison the entire workflow if the system does not recognize that risk explicitly. This task introduces the deterministic source-quality checks and fallback rules described in the plan.

Scope:
- Score parse quality using simple, testable heuristics such as content size, heading density, table presence, missing sections, and garble indicators.
- Map poor quality to explicit degrade or clarification-first recommendations.
- Keep the logic deterministic and easy to test.

Deliverables:
- Parse-quality classifier and policy outputs for each current snapshot.
- A rule set that later readiness and orchestration logic can consume.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Low-quality primary inputs are surfaced before they silently contaminate canonical extraction.
- The workflow can distinguish between acceptable degradation and true halt conditions.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Guidance:
- Avoid sophisticated heuristics that are hard to explain. This layer's value comes from transparency and repeatability.

title: Render authoritative source-manifest artifacts for each run
description:
Background:
The source manifest is the first durable audit artifact of a run. This task converts normalized rows, snapshots, and quality states into the canonical `01-source-manifest` outputs.

Scope:
- Render both markdown and JSON manifest outputs.
- Include type, priority, snapshot linkage, quality state, freshness, status, and later screen usage hooks.
- Make the artifact clear enough for humans to inspect and for other workflow steps to consume programmatically.

Deliverables:
- `01-source-manifest.md` and `01-source-manifest.json` generation logic.
- Stable output contract for later audits and validations.

Acceptance Criteria:
- A run produces a consistent manifest artifact that later stages and humans can trust.
- The manifest captures enough context that future reruns can explain what changed.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Future-self note:
- This artifact will often be the first thing someone reads when questioning a run. Optimize it for clarity and traceability rather than terse machine-only structure.

title: Phase 2: build canonical extraction, evidence linkage, and gap analysis
description:
Background:
This phase is the conceptual heart of the upgrade. It turns NotebookLM from a generic answer engine into a workflow-native extractor that produces stable terminology, screen catalogs, per-screen canonical facts, and explicit blockers rather than freeform prose.

Scope:
- Establish prompt and parse utilities that can safely degrade without hiding failure.
- Normalize citations into evidence objects linked to stored snapshots.
- Generate terminology, screen catalogs, canonical data, and structured gap classification.

Deliverables:
- Prompt registry and structured ask utilities.
- Evidence normalization and snapshot-linked canonical extraction outputs.
- Terminology map, screen catalog, canonical JSON, and gap backlogs.

## Success Criteria
- Every confirmed fact in canonical outputs can point back to evidence.
- Contradictions and missing information are preserved explicitly instead of being smoothed over in narrative text.
- The repo has a stable per-screen truth layer for rendering and readiness logic.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Sequencing note:
- The project begins to differentiate itself here. If this phase is weak, later renderers will simply be formatting ungrounded prose.
- Do not collapse contradictions prematurely. Preserving competing claims is a feature, not a bug.

title: Implement a prompt registry and structured-ask utilities with degraded JSON handling
description:
Background:
Canonical extraction will require repeated, high-signal asks with reusable prompt shapes. This task creates the prompt registry and parse-recovery helpers needed to keep those asks reproducible and robust against imperfect JSON output.

Scope:
- Create named prompt templates for extraction, contradiction review, readiness review, and related workflow operations.
- Implement the degraded parsing ladder described in the plan: parse as-is, fenced JSON extraction, first valid span extraction, then degraded raw-text return.
- Return machine-readable parse quality states instead of collapsing all failure into exceptions.

Deliverables:
- Prompt registry, structured ask helper surface, and parsing fallback utilities.
- Tests covering valid JSON, fenced JSON, partial JSON, and degraded text-only cases.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Later extraction tasks can reuse a stable structured-ask primitive rather than hand-rolling prompts and parsing logic.
- Imperfect JSON no longer forces the whole workflow to choose between crash or silent misuse.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Future-self guidance:
- Narrow, screen-scoped asks are part of the safety model. Do not drift back toward giant omnibus prompts just because they feel convenient.

title: Normalize citations into snapshot-linked evidence objects
description:
Background:
The workflow's evidence-first guarantee depends on turning NotebookLM citation output into stable evidence records that point to the exact source snapshots used during extraction. This task creates that bridge.

Scope:
- Normalize whatever citation shape NotebookLM exposes into a single internal evidence object.
- Link each evidence object to source keys and snapshot identities.
- Preserve human-friendly locator information while keeping the data machine-usable.

Deliverables:
- Evidence normalization utilities and schema-compatible outputs.
- Tests proving evidence linkage remains stable across runs and reruns.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Canonical facts can carry traceable evidence regardless of variation in raw NotebookLM citation format.
- Later validation can inspect evidence without depending on raw response structure.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Rationale:
- This is one of the most important seams in the entire design. If evidence objects are loose or unstable, 'grounded' outputs will be performative rather than real.

title: Implement terminology normalization and ambiguity tracking
description:
Background:
Vocabulary drift is a common cause of downstream FE/BE misunderstanding. This task stabilizes terminology before screen-level extraction begins and records ambiguity instead of pretending conflicting terms mean the same thing.

Scope:
- Extract terminology candidates from the relevant source set.
- Normalize aliases only when there is evidence to support the merge.
- Emit explicit ambiguity records when business terms conflict or remain unclear.

Deliverables:
- Terminology JSON/markdown outputs and ambiguity flags.
- Logic for reusing the terminology map in later extraction and rendering steps.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Later screens and matrices can reference a stable vocabulary layer.
- Ambiguous terminology is visible early instead of leaking into contradictory downstream docs.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Guidance:
- Over-normalization is dangerous. Preserve ambiguity if the evidence is weak; clarity can be added later via note-derived clarifications or resolved requirements.

title: Implement stable screen-catalog extraction and screen-ID policy
description:
Background:
The workflow needs a stable, diffable understanding of the feature's screens, roles, entry points, exits, and primary actions. This task converts requirement material into a screen catalog with stable IDs suitable for rerun targeting.

Scope:
- Extract screens and flows from the relevant source set using the terminology and evidence layers.
- Define a stable screen-ID generation policy that survives reruns unless the underlying screen meaning truly changes.
- Capture open questions and evidence at the catalog level.

Deliverables:
- `02-screen-catalog.json` generation and stable ID policy.
- Tests for catalog stability across harmless reruns and deliberate material changes.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The workflow can reason about the feature screen-by-screen instead of treating the whole BA set as one blob.
- Later impacted-screen reruns have a trustworthy target set to work with.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Future-self note:
- Stable IDs are not cosmetic. They determine whether reruns are cheap and whether changelogs are intelligible.

title: Implement the per-screen canonical extraction engine
description:
Background:
This task creates the actual canonical truth layer for each screen: shared facts, FE facts, BE facts, dependencies, contradictions, missing info, and quality summaries. It is the central data product of the BA runner.

Scope:
- Extract screen-scoped canonical facts using the prompt registry, evidence normalization, terminology map, and screen catalog.
- Represent fact status explicitly as confirmed, provisional, missing, contradicted, or inferred.
- Require evidence for confirmed facts and explicit rationale for provisional or inferred facts.

Deliverables:
- Per-screen `canonical.json` generation with the schema described in the plan.
- Unit/integration coverage proving the extraction engine preserves evidence and contradictory claims correctly.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The repo has a durable per-screen truth layer that later renderers and validators can depend on.
- No fact can accidentally masquerade as confirmed without evidence.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Critical-path reminder:
- This task is the heart of the upgrade. If it is watered down into a thin wrapper around prose answers, the rest of the design collapses.

title: Implement gap, contradiction, blocker, and question classification
description:
Background:
The workflow must distinguish between kinds of uncertainty rather than flattening everything into 'needs clarification.' This task formalizes the blocker and question taxonomy that later readiness logic depends on.

Scope:
- Classify missing requirement detail, contradictory requirement detail, missing backend contract information, FE-visible dependencies, and deferred implementation detail separately.
- Emit structured blocker/question records with owner and severity where possible.
- Preserve contradiction backlogs instead of collapsing them away.

Deliverables:
- Gap-review outputs suitable for readiness calculation and `questions.md` rendering.
- Tests that show the classifier separates materially different uncertainty types.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Readiness logic can rely on explicit blocker categories rather than prose interpretation.
- Open questions remain actionable and auditable.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Guidance:
- The point of this task is operational clarity. FE teams can work with some missing backend detail but not with hidden contradictions masquerading as certainty.

title: Phase 3: render deterministic FE/BE outputs and FE-first deliverables
description:
Background:
Once the canonical layer exists, the workflow needs to turn it into the actual artifacts the business cares about: FE specs, BE specs, matrices, readiness decisions, provisional contracts, mock data, and the final output tree. This phase is where the runner starts to feel useful to downstream implementers.

Scope:
- Generate all downstream artifacts from canonical state rather than raw chat prose.
- Support FE-first execution honestly through readiness logic, provisional contracts, and aligned mock data.
- Assemble the output tree in a deterministic, repeatable layout.

Deliverables:
- Matrix generation, readiness evaluation, FE/BE renderers, contracts, mock data, and bundle assembly.
- Stable markdown/JSON/YAML/CSV artifacts under the planned directory structure.

## Success Criteria
- FE and BE docs can be regenerated from canonical state without manual prompt surgery.
- FE-first scenarios emit clearly provisional contracts and matching mock data when backend interactions are present.
- The output bundle is complete enough for later orchestration and validation work.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Future-self guidance:
- This is the point where polished-looking output becomes dangerous if it is not grounded. Keep renderers deterministic and keep provisional markers conspicuous.
- The goal is not literary quality. The goal is traceable, implementation-ready structure.

title: Generate field, action-rule, and API matrices from canonical state
description:
Background:
The workflow needs structured matrices that implementers can inspect directly and validators can check mechanically. This task derives those matrices from canonical facts and focused extraction rather than forcing agents to assemble them by hand.

Scope:
- Generate field, action-rule, and API matrices with evidence traceability.
- Allow draft assistance from NotebookLM data-table outputs only if the final saved CSVs pass schema checks.
- Keep matrix generation deterministic at the point of publication.

Deliverables:
- Matrix generation logic and output contracts for CSV artifacts.
- Schema validation for matrix rows.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The workflow can emit machine-checkable matrices tied back to canonical facts.
- Later renderers and validators can reason about matrix content without reparsing prose.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Future-self note:
- Matrices are not filler. They are one of the easiest places to detect omissions and contradictions early.

title: Implement mode selection and readiness evaluation with per-screen overrides
description:
Background:
The workflow must decide whether a feature is ready for balanced FE/BE work, FE-first work, clarification-first work, or not ready. This task turns canonical data and blocker classification into explicit readiness decisions, including the hybrid per-screen behavior described in the plan.

Scope:
- Implement `AUTO`, `BALANCED`, `FE_FIRST`, and `CLARIFICATION_FIRST` logic.
- Support feature-level mode plus per-screen overrides where the evidence justifies it.
- Produce explicit readiness enums and the rationale behind them.

Deliverables:
- Readiness engine and structured readiness outputs.
- Tests proving degraded parse quality, missing contracts, and contradictions lower readiness appropriately.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The workflow can state what is ready, what is blocked, and why.
- Hybrid screen-by-screen mode selection is possible without losing feature-level coherence.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Guidance:
- Keep the system honest. Readiness should drop when evidence quality drops, even if that makes the output less pleasant.

title: Render FE specifications deterministically from canonical state
description:
Background:
FE implementers need structured, screen-specific specs that inherit the canonical layer's evidence and uncertainty handling. This task renders the FE-facing markdown from canonical state, matrices, and readiness outputs.

Scope:
- Render screen purpose, states, fields, validations, actions, visible business rules, loading/error/empty states, API references, and open FE questions.
- Preserve provisional markers explicitly where FE-first assumptions are in play.
- Keep the renderer deterministic so reruns are diffable and testable.

Deliverables:
- Per-screen `fe.md` renderer and tests.

Acceptance Criteria:
- FE docs can be regenerated from canonical data with stable structure.
- Visible FE uncertainty is preserved rather than hidden in prose flourishes.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Future-self note:
- FE specs are where overconfidence is especially risky. A clean markdown file must not imply more backend certainty than the canonical layer actually supports.

title: Render BE specifications and per-screen question backlogs from canonical state
description:
Background:
BE implementers and reviewers need the same grounded discipline as FE outputs, plus a durable question backlog for unresolved requirements. This task renders BE-facing markdown and question backlogs from structured state.

Scope:
- Render entities, workflows, endpoints/events/jobs, validation rules, permissions notes where evidenced, contradictions, and open BE questions.
- Aggregate `questions.md` content from missing, contradicted, and owner-routed questions.
- Keep output deterministic and traceable to the canonical layer.

Deliverables:
- Per-screen `be.md` and `questions.md` renderers.

Acceptance Criteria:
- BE docs and question backlogs are derived from the same canonical state as FE docs.
- Outstanding uncertainty remains visible and owner-routable.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Guidance:
- Do not let the question backlog become a dumping ground. It should preserve actionable uncertainty with enough structure for ownership and follow-up.

title: Generate provisional OpenAPI contracts for FE-first screens
description:
Background:
FE-first execution only becomes practical if the workflow can emit contracts that are explicit about uncertainty instead of forcing FE teams to invent their own assumptions. This task generates those provisional contracts from canonical state and readiness decisions.

Scope:
- Emit OpenAPI 3.0.3 contracts where FE-first work needs backend interaction definitions.
- Mark provisional endpoints and fields clearly using explicit vendor extensions and metadata.
- Carry evidence and open-question context into contract metadata where useful.

Deliverables:
- Per-screen or per-feature provisional contract generation.
- Validation that contract metadata preserves provisional status clearly.

Acceptance Criteria:
- FE-first runs can produce machine-usable contracts without pretending they are approved backend truth.
- Contract uncertainty is discoverable by both humans and tooling.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Future-self warning:
- The main risk here is social, not technical: downstream users may mistake generated contracts for approved ones. Make the provisional status impossible to miss.

title: Generate deterministic mock data aligned to provisional contracts
description:
Background:
Mock payloads are the practical companion to FE-first contracts. This task generates deterministic fixtures that align to provisional contract shape and cover the baseline UI states the plan calls for.

Scope:
- Generate at least happy-path, validation-error, empty-state, and server-error mock data.
- Keep generation deterministic so diffs and tests are meaningful.
- Validate mocks against the provisional contract shape.

Deliverables:
- `mock-data.json` generation logic and contract-alignment checks.

Acceptance Criteria:
- FE consumers receive usable mock payloads whenever the workflow emits provisional contracts.
- Contract and mock-data drift is mechanically catchable.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Guidance:
- Mock-data usefulness depends on alignment, not creativity. Favor stable, representative fixtures over elaborate randomization.

title: Assemble the deterministic bundle renderer and final output layout
description:
Background:
The individual renderers are only useful if the run can materialize the complete, coherent output tree promised by the plan. This task assembles the overview, readiness summary, per-screen outputs, and run metadata into the final layout.

Scope:
- Render `00-overview.md`, `03-readiness-summary.md`, and the per-screen directory structure from structured state.
- Place matrices, contracts, mock data, QA outputs, and run artifacts in the expected layout.
- Keep rendering deterministic and file-presence rules mode-aware.

Deliverables:
- Bundle assembly logic for the documented output tree.
- Tests that assert output presence/absence by mode and feature state.

Acceptance Criteria:
- A run can write the full output tree in a way that later validation and rerun logic can rely on.
- The output layout is stable enough for docs, fixtures, and downstream tooling.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Future-self note:
- The output tree is part of the product contract. Once it starts drifting casually, every downstream consumer pays the cost.

title: Phase 4: orchestrate the pipeline and support selective reruns
description:
Background:
A workflow-native product is more than a set of callable primitives. This phase turns the discrete steps into a stateful pipeline with progress reporting, resumability, and cheap reruns when upstream sources change.

Scope:
- Persist execution state and expose a coherent `ba.*` tool surface.
- Drive the full pipeline through a single orchestration macro.
- Support source-diff-driven impacted reruns and human-readable changelog output.

Deliverables:
- State machine, public MCP handlers, end-to-end pipeline macro, status surfaces, and rerun logic.

## Success Criteria
- A caller can start a run, inspect progress, resume if needed, and rerun only impacted screens after source changes.
- The workflow exposes halt reasons and degraded states rather than forcing the caller to infer them from raw logs.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Sequencing note:
- Orchestration should not paper over weak underlying steps. If a sub-phase is still soft, the pipeline must surface that honestly instead of smearing uncertainty across the whole run.
- Rerun economics are part of the product value, not an optimization after the fact.

title: Implement a persisted run state machine and audit trail for BA workflow execution
description:
Background:
End-to-end orchestration needs explicit execution state, halt reasons, retries, degraded states, and resumability. This task defines the run-state machinery that lets the BA runner behave like a real workflow engine rather than a long helper function.

Scope:
- Define execution states and persisted step-level metadata.
- Record audit events and halt reasons in the run store.
- Support resumability without losing clarity about what has and has not completed.

Deliverables:
- State machine implementation with persisted run-step records.
- Audit/event schema and tests for transitions and degraded states.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Later orchestration tools can reason about run state explicitly.
- Interrupted or degraded runs remain inspectable instead of becoming opaque failure blobs.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Guidance:
- Keep state explicit and finite. 'Best effort' hidden transitions make reruns and debugging much harder than they look at first.

title: Establish shared `ba.*` tool registration, payload conventions, and thin MCP wrappers
description:
Background:
The BA runner needs a single shared MCP seam for the `ba.*` workflow surface so callers see consistent naming, payload envelopes, and error behavior. Individual workflow semantics should still live in their phase-specific beads rather than being reimplemented in one giant registration task.

Scope:
- Establish shared registration helpers, parameter/result conventions, and common MCP wrapper patterns for the `ba.*` surface.
- Register thin public wrappers around the underlying BA workflow operations as those operations become available.
- Keep step-specific orchestration, status, and rerun logic in their dedicated implementation beads instead of centralizing product behavior here.

Deliverables:
- Shared `ba.*` registration/contract helpers and thin MCP wrappers.
- Contract-level tests covering naming, result envelopes, and error mapping consistency.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The BA surface uses one coherent naming and payload convention across tools.
- Later step-specific tools can plug into the same layer without bespoke MCP glue.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Future-self warning:
- Public tools are expensive commitments. Keep the surface meaningful and avoid exposing every internal helper just because it exists.

comments.author: Codex
comments.text: Planning revision: this bead now explicitly covers shared BA-tool MCP plumbing only. Step-specific product behavior remains owned by the phase beads that implement those semantics.

title: Implement the end-to-end `ba.run_pipeline` orchestration macro
description:
Background:
The BA runner's main value proposition is that agents do not need to manually remember the full sequence of source prep, extraction, rendering, and validation steps. This task turns the discrete pieces into a single macro that executes the documented pipeline coherently.

Scope:
- Wire the ordered workflow steps into one pipeline operation with step-level progress and halt reporting.
- Support dry-run mode that stops after readiness assessment.
- Ensure failures are surfaced with explicit step identity and structured state updates.

Deliverables:
- `ba.run_pipeline` implementation with progress/state integration.
- Tests exercising successful, degraded, and halted runs.

Acceptance Criteria:
- A caller can execute the full BA workflow through one coherent entry point.
- The orchestration does not hide which step failed or why the run degraded.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Sequencing rationale:
- This task should compose stable underlying phases, not compensate for unfinished ones. If a step is still soft, the macro should reflect that honestly.

title: Implement `ba.status` progress, resumability semantics, and run inspection surfaces
description:
Background:
Workflow runners are only practical if callers can inspect what is happening without reading logs or poking around the filesystem. This task exposes `ba.status` on top of the persisted run state so status, progress, and resume safety are explicit.

Scope:
- Expose `ba.status` with run status, current step, completed steps, degraded states, and halt reasons.
- Support resumability semantics where safe and clearly indicate what resume means.
- Keep caller-visible status aligned with the persisted state machine rather than deriving it heuristically.

Deliverables:
- `ba.status` surface with tests.
- Resumability semantics that are documented and deterministic.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Operators can see where a run is and whether it is safe to continue, resume, or inspect failures.
- No caller needs to infer run progress from side effects on disk.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Guidance:
- Make resumability conservative. It is better to restart a step honestly than to imply resume safety where state is ambiguous.

title: Implement `ba.rerun_impacted`: snapshot diffing, impact mapping, selective reruns, and changelog output
description:
Background:
Cheap reruns are one of the strongest practical advantages of this design. This task powers `ba.rerun_impacted` by comparing source snapshots, mapping changed content back to screens using evidence links and terminology, rerunning only what changed, and emitting a changelog for humans.

Scope:
- Diff old and new source snapshots using content hashes, headings, spans, and terminology changes.
- Map diffs to candidate screens using screen catalogs, evidence links, and matrix references.
- Rerun impacted screens plus dependent summaries and emit a human-readable changelog.

Deliverables:
- `ba.rerun_impacted`, selective rerun engine, `impacted-screens.json`, and `changelog.md` generation.
- Tests proving harmless reruns stay narrow while cross-cutting changes escalate correctly.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The workflow can update only affected screens instead of rerunning the entire feature by default.
- Rerun output explains what changed and what remains provisional.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Future-self note:
- This is where the earlier investments in source keys, snapshot IDs, screen IDs, and evidence objects start paying for themselves. If those are weak, this task will turn into guesswork.

title: Phase 5: harden the workflow with validation, fixtures, canaries, and metrics
description:
Background:
This phase converts a plausible workflow into one that can be trusted over time. It adds bundle validation, safe deterministic repair, realistic fixtures, golden files, canaries for upstream drift, and operational success metrics.

Scope:
- Validate artifact invariants and evidence integrity.
- Add fixture-driven and gold-file-driven regression coverage.
- Detect NotebookLM/MCP drift early and measure whether the workflow is actually reducing manual effort.

Deliverables:
- Validator, safe repair rules, realistic fixtures, golden tests, canary coverage, and metrics instrumentation.

## Success Criteria
- The bundle validator catches missing evidence, inconsistent statuses, contract/mock mismatches, and overconfident readiness outcomes.
- Representative fixtures exercise happy-path, degraded, contradictory, and rerun scenarios.
- Operational metrics exist so the team can judge whether the workflow delivers real downstream value.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Future-self note:
- This phase is what stops the project from becoming a strong demo with weak trust economics.
- Keep self-repair narrow: formatting and deterministic consistency fixes are fine; invented evidence is not.

title: Implement bundle validator invariants and `qa-report.json` generation
description:
Background:
The workflow needs a final checkpoint that verifies the bundle is internally consistent and still grounded. This task implements the invariant checks described in the plan and emits structured QA results.

Scope:
- Validate evidence presence, canonical/rendered alignment, readiness consistency, contract/mock alignment, terminology consistency, and required file presence.
- Emit a structured `qa-report.json` plus pass/fail/warning summary.
- Block publish on meaningful validation failures unless explicitly overridden.

Deliverables:
- Bundle validator and QA report outputs.
- Tests covering the major failure classes from the plan.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The workflow can detect missing evidence, inconsistent statuses, and false readiness before outputs are treated as trustworthy.
- QA results are machine-readable and suitable for automation or review.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Guidance:
- Validator credibility matters. Favor checks that are explainable and tied directly to the workflow contract over opaque scoring.

title: Implement safe deterministic self-repair for non-semantic bundle failures
description:
Background:
Some validation failures are safe to repair automatically, such as formatting or deterministic consistency mismatches. This task implements those narrow repair paths while explicitly avoiding any repair that would invent missing evidence or hidden assumptions.

Scope:
- Define which QA failures are eligible for deterministic repair and which must remain hard failures.
- Implement repair logic for safe cases only.
- Record when a repair occurred so the audit trail remains honest.

Deliverables:
- Safe repair policy and implementation.
- Tests demonstrating that evidence-free or ambiguity-heavy failures remain unrepaired.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The workflow can auto-fix deterministic presentation issues without claiming to resolve semantic uncertainty.
- Repair behavior is explicit and auditable.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Future-self warning:
- Self-repair is a sharp tool. The default failure mode should still be to surface uncertainty, not to make the report look cleaner than it is.

title: Build representative BA fixture suites for happy-path, degraded, contradiction, rerun, and note-derived scenarios
description:
Background:
The revised plan explicitly calls for realistic fixtures that cover the workflow's hardest cases. This task creates and organizes those fixture sets so the pipeline can be regression-tested against known conditions rather than demos alone.

Scope:
- Create the six representative fixture families from the plan: clean, missing-contract, contradictory, garbled, rerun-diff, and note-derived clarification.
- Make the fixtures rich enough to exercise source intelligence, canonical extraction, rendering, and rerun logic meaningfully.
- Keep fixture organization understandable for future contributors.

Deliverables:
- Fixture data and helper utilities for integration/golden tests.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The repo contains realistic, reusable BA fixtures that cover both success and failure modes.
- Later tests can target known workflow behaviors rather than ad hoc synthetic one-offs.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Guidance:
- Invest in fixtures that reveal real workflow weaknesses. The goal is not high fixture count; it is broad behavioral coverage with understandable artifacts.

title: Add golden-file coverage for canonical outputs, rendered docs, and readiness summaries
description:
Background:
Once fixture inputs exist, the repo needs stable expected outputs to detect regressions in canonical structure and rendering behavior. This task adds that gold-file coverage.

Scope:
- Capture golden canonical JSON, FE/BE docs, readiness summaries, and changelog outputs where appropriate.
- Make update ergonomics clear so future contributors can tell when a golden diff is intentional versus a regression.
- Use goldens to protect deterministic renderer behavior and key extraction invariants.

Deliverables:
- Golden-file tests and maintenance guidance.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Core workflow outputs are regression-protected.
- Contributors can review output changes intentionally instead of discovering drift after the fact.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Future-self note:
- Goldens are only useful if they stay readable. Favor fixture/output organization that makes diffs reviewable by humans.

title: Add upstream canary and smoke coverage for NotebookLM and MCP drift
description:
Background:
Because the project rides undocumented NotebookLM APIs, the workflow needs early warning when upstream behavior changes. This task adds canary and smoke coverage targeted at the surfaces the BA runner depends on most.

Scope:
- Exercise the highest-risk upstream paths with lightweight smoke/canary checks.
- Focus on capability drift that would break source retrieval, chat extraction, notes, settings, or artifact helpers used by the runner.
- Keep the suite cheap enough to run regularly.

Deliverables:
- Canary/smoke tests and documentation for how to interpret failures.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The repo can detect important upstream drift before the workflow silently degrades in production use.
- Canary failures point to concrete capability areas rather than a generic 'NotebookLM changed' message.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Guidance:
- Keep canaries narrow and informative. Their job is early warning, not exhaustive end-to-end confidence.

title: Instrument operational metrics and evaluation reporting for workflow usefulness
description:
Background:
The revised plan defines success partly in operational terms: manual edits per screen, rerun savings, time-to-first-spec, and caught ungrounded facts. This task instruments the workflow so those claims can be measured rather than assumed.

Scope:
- Record the workflow metrics called out in the plan or the closest practical proxies.
- Keep metrics local-first and aligned with the non-sharing scope.
- Expose enough reporting that future evaluation can compare workflow improvements over time.

Deliverables:
- Metrics capture and reporting hooks.
- Documentation explaining what each metric means and how to interpret it.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The team can tell whether the workflow is actually reducing manual effort and rerun cost.
- Metrics do not compromise the local-first, non-sharing assumptions of the project.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Future-self note:
- Shipping the runner without measurement makes it too easy to confuse architectural elegance with practical usefulness.

title: Phase 6: complete high-value parity and fence optional artifacts behind stability rules
description:
Background:
After the core BA runner exists, the repo should expose the remaining non-sharing capabilities that materially help the workflow while keeping unstable or low-value artifact helpers off the critical path. This phase is about disciplined completeness, not feature sprawl.

Scope:
- Expose parity helpers that directly improve curation, configuration, or draft generation.
- Mark unstable or low-value artifacts as optional/experimental rather than silently normalizing them into the critical path.

Deliverables:
- Notes/source conversion helpers, output language/settings parity, report/data-table helpers, mind map export, and experimental non-core artifact helpers.

## Success Criteria
- Optional parity expands the server cleanly without diluting the BA-runner mental model.
- Experimental artifacts are clearly marked and documented as non-blocking to the primary workflow.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Sequencing note:
- This phase should not steal focus from the runner itself. If priorities collide, core workflow trust wins over breadth.
- The purpose of optional parity is operator leverage and completeness, not vanity feature count.

title: Expose notes-to-source and curated-source helpers for clarification loops
description:
Background:
The revised plan treats NotebookLM notes as a controlled curation loop, not an informal side channel. This task exposes the note/source helpers needed to turn clarifications and decisions into typed workflow inputs.

Scope:
- Expose note creation/export/source-conversion helpers relevant to clarification and decision capture.
- Tag note-derived sources distinctly from original requirement sources.
- Keep note-derived sources from silently overwriting contradictory primary evidence.

Deliverables:
- MCP helpers for note-based curation workflows and tests.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The workflow can ingest curated clarifications as explicit supporting sources.
- Manual decisions become durable, typed inputs rather than tribal memory.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Guidance:
- The value here is controlled curation. Do not let note-derived material blur the distinction between primary requirements and later clarifications.

title: Expose output language and settings parity needed by the BA workflow
description:
Background:
Some workflow use cases need control over NotebookLM output settings, especially language and related chat settings. This task exposes the parts of that surface that materially support the BA runner.

Scope:
- Expose output language and relevant settings in a way that the BA runner can consume or pass through safely.
- Keep the public interface aligned with existing settings semantics where possible.

Deliverables:
- Settings parity helpers and tests for the workflow-relevant subset.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The BA runner can control or surface language/settings when needed without resorting to hidden configuration assumptions.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Future-self note:
- Scope this to workflow-relevant settings first. The goal is leverage, not a maximal settings mirror for its own sake.

title: Expose report and data-table helpers for structured drafting assistance
description:
Background:
Reports and data tables are among the highest-value parity helpers for this workflow because they can assist structured drafting without becoming the final system of record. This task exposes those helpers cleanly.

Scope:
- Expose report/data-table capability through parity helpers or adapter support where it materially helps the BA runner.
- Keep draft-assistance status clear so downstream code does not mistake these artifacts for authoritative final output.

Deliverables:
- Report/data-table helper surface and tests.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The workflow can use report/data-table assistance where helpful without making those artifacts the canonical truth layer.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Guidance:
- These helpers are best treated as accelerators feeding structured pipelines, not as final outputs to trust blindly.

title: Expose mind map export and stability guards for non-core artifact helpers
description:
Background:
Mind maps can help with topic coverage and onboarding, but they are not critical-path implementation artifacts. This task exposes mind map support while also defining the guardrails that keep non-core artifact helpers from quietly entering the core workflow path.

Scope:
- Expose mind map export or retrieval support as parity functionality.
- Define stability and critical-path guardrails for non-core artifact helpers.

Deliverables:
- Mind map parity helper and artifact-policy hooks/documentation.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Useful non-core artifact support is available without becoming an accidental workflow dependency.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Future-self note:
- The guardrail is as important as the helper. The repo should make it obvious that mind maps are optional aids, not required workflow outputs.

title: Expose optional audio, video, slide, and infographic helpers behind explicit experimental flags
description:
Background:
The repository can offer broader artifact parity for completeness, but those helpers should remain visibly optional because they are long-running, variably stable, and off the BA runner's critical path. This task adds them under explicit experimental boundaries.

Scope:
- Expose optional audio/video/slide/infographic helpers where the underlying SDK support is real enough to justify parity.
- Gate them with explicit experimental labeling or flags.
- Keep them clearly outside the core BA-runner path.

Deliverables:
- Experimental parity helpers and associated docs/config notes.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The server offers broad optional parity without implying these artifact helpers are required or production-stable for the BA workflow.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Guidance:
- Optional parity should be additive, not distracting. If the implementation starts bending core abstractions to serve these helpers, the boundary is wrong.

title: Documentation and contributor enablement for the BA runner
description:
Background:
The workflow upgrade changes the public MCP surface, the repository architecture, the expected output tree, and the testing model. This epic tracks the documentation and contributor-facing guidance needed to keep the implementation understandable after the initial push.

Scope:
- Document the BA workflow itself, the public tool contracts, and the output bundle contract.
- Update user-facing docs and examples so the MCP surface does not drift from implementation reality.
- Explain fixtures, canaries, reruns, and contributor expectations so future maintenance stays coherent.

Deliverables:
- Workflow guide, public MCP docs, examples, and contributor/testing notes.

## Success Criteria
- A new contributor can understand what the BA runner is, how to invoke it, what outputs to expect, and how to extend it safely.
- Public docs distinguish core workflow tools from optional parity and experimental helpers.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Future-self note:
- Documentation is part of the product contract here. If the docs lag badly, the public MCP surface will look more arbitrary than it is and contributors will start reintroducing hidden assumptions.

title: Write the BA workflow guide and output-bundle contract documentation
description:
Background:
The workflow changes the shape of the MCP product. This task documents how the BA runner operates, what it accepts, what it outputs, and how to interpret degraded states and readiness outcomes.

Scope:
- Document the BA workflow inputs, modes, outputs, rerun behavior, and validation semantics.
- Document the output directory contract in a way that future contributors and operators can rely on.

Deliverables:
- Workflow guide and output-bundle contract docs.

Acceptance Criteria:
- A reader can understand the workflow end to end without reverse-engineering the code.
- The documented output layout matches implementation reality.

comments.author: FoggyOwl
comments.text:
Future-self note:
- This guide should explain not only what the workflow does when everything goes well, but also what degraded, blocked, and provisional states mean in practice.

title: Update README, MCP tool reference, and runnable examples for the BA runner surface
description:
Background:
